# Appeal of Denial – Rotator Cuff Repair (CPT 29827)

**RE: Appeal of Adverse Benefit Determination**
**Member:** Riley Brooks
**Member ID:** W997409334
**Denial date:** 2026-08-09
**Reference number:** POC-AA9EA32E7D-95281
**Governing policy:** Molina Clinical Policy MCP-404 Shoulder Arthroscopy (Original Effective 6/9/21; Revision 6/9/21), https://www.molinahealthcare.com/-/media/Molina/PublicWebsite/PDF/Providers/il/resource/Shoulder-Arthroscopy-Guidelines_MCP_404.pdf

Dear Molina Healthcare,

I am appealing the denial of my prior authorization request for rotator cuff repair (CPT 29827), referenced above. My surgeon, Dr. Reyes, has documented that this procedure is medically necessary, and I am asking Molina to reconsider this denial.

## Why this denial should be reconsidered

The denial states that "the clinical records submitted do not document an adequate trial of conservative treatment prior to the requested surgery." Molina's own policy, MCP-404, sets out what conservative treatment must look like before shoulder surgery is considered. The relevant language from that policy states:

> "Diagnostic arthroscopy may be considered medically necessary when ALL of the following criteria are met:"

> " Severe, disabling pain and/or a documented loss of shoulder function which interferes with the ability to carry out age appropriate activities of daily living;"

> "and  Failure of non-surgical management for at least three (3) months in duration including at least two of the following as appropriate:"

My records show the following:

- **Duration and severity of symptoms:** I had 12 months of progressive shoulder pain that did not improve with rest, and I cannot lift my arm above shoulder height or sleep on the affected side. This documents "severe, disabling pain and/or a documented loss of shoulder function which interferes with the ability to carry out age appropriate activities of daily living," as the policy describes.

- **Failure of non-surgical management for at least three months:** I completed 12 weeks of supervised physical therapy focused on rotator cuff strengthening and scapular mechanics (2026-04-01 to 2026-06-24, 16 visits), as documented in my physical therapy discharge note. I also used NSAIDs for 6 months with inadequate relief, and received a corticosteroid injection on 2026-05-19 that gave only 4 weeks of partial relief. This is more than the three-month minimum the policy requires, and it includes more than the two forms of non-surgical management the policy asks for ("at least two of the following as appropriate").

- **Objective findings:** An MRI on 2026-06-16 showed a full-thickness supraspinatus tear measuring 1.8 cm with grade 2 fatty atrophy. On examination, I had positive provocative testing and range of motion limited by pain.

I note that the excerpts provided to me from MCP-404 set out general criteria for shoulder arthroscopy (including the pain/function and conservative-care requirements quoted above), but the specific subsection addressing rotator cuff repair itself was not included in what I was given. I am asking Molina to confirm which subsection of MCP-404 was applied to CPT 29827 specifically, and to show how my records were measured against it.

## Request for the criteria applied

Molina's utilization management materials state that criteria used for review are MCG guidelines available through the secure provider portal, and that members may call to obtain the criteria used to make a final determination. I am requesting, in writing, the MCG guideline title and criteria applied to my determination, so that I and my surgeon can review exactly what standard was used and respond to it directly.

## What I am asking Molina to do

I am asking Molina Healthcare to reconsider and overturn the denial of CPT 29827, rotator cuff repair, based on the conservative treatment I completed and the findings documented in my records. I understand this letter does not guarantee that the denial will be overturned, but I believe the record shows that the plan's own published conservative-care requirements have been met.

## Deadline and submission

I understand this appeal must be received by 2027-02-05. I am submitting it through the Molina member portal at molinahealthcare.com and by phone using the Member Services number on my ID card, and I am mailing this letter to the appeal address printed on my denial letter, since that address is authoritative.

Please confirm receipt of this appeal and let me know if any additional information is needed.

Sincerely,

**Riley Brooks**
Member ID: W997409334
[Address]
[Phone number]
[Email address]
[Date]

---

*This letter is not medical or legal advice and does not guarantee that coverage will be approved.*
